item.text:
**Bottom Line**  
6B.1 is mixed but leans negative. Tshisekedi’s 2024 record does contain real welfare-oriented moves, especially in education and some social spending, and he did keep peace/de-escalation language in play. But the stronger evidence says human welfare was not the core organizing purpose of rule in practice: public resources remained underprovided or misused, conflict and emergency rule dominated, and civilians faced severe abuses that the state did not prevent.

**Accepted Claims**
- **Strengthening Public Social Spending in DRC** — IMF, 2024-07-15, https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/227/article-A002-en.xml  
  - Claim: The IMF said social spending had increased and education and health were prioritized, including free primary education, but social protection remained very small and budget credibility was still weak. This is real welfare-oriented policy, but only partial and not yet transformative.  
  - IDs: `6B.1`, `5B.8`, `5B.6`, `5B.10`

- **Democratic Republic of Congo: Expanding and Equipping Primary School Classrooms for Better Learning Outcomes** — World Bank, 2024-02-26, https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/02/28/democratic-republic-of-congo-afe-expanding-and-equipping-primary-school-classrooms-for-better-learning-outcomes  
  - Claim: The project explicitly aimed to improve learning conditions, build and equip classrooms, support girls and students with disabilities, strengthen teacher quality, and improve decentralized planning. This is strong evidence that at least some policy capacity was being directed toward human development, not only patronage or rhetoric.  
  - IDs: `6B.1`, `5B.6`, `5B.8`

- **Crise sécuritaire dans l’Est de la RDC: les présidents Félix Tshisekedi et Salva Kiir appellent au respect des accords de paix** — Présidence RDC, 2024-03-25, https://presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/crise_securitaire_dans_lest_de_la_rdc_les_presidents_felix_tshisekedi_et_salva_kiir_appellent_au-respect_des_accords_de_paix  
  - Claim: Tshisekedi publicly called for relaunching the Nairobi and Luanda peace processes and said he would spare no effort to restore peace, security, and stability. That is welfare-relevant because it treats civilian safety and de-escalation as politically meaningful, though it is still more crisis diplomacy than a full human-welfare agenda.  
  - IDs: `6B.1`, `5B.7`, `5B.9`, `5B.10`

- **DRC: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis** — Amnesty International, 2024-06-24, https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/  
  - Claim: Amnesty said Tshisekedi had made many human-rights pledges, but there had been little to no progress; it also said public resources were being squandered, leaving essential services underfunded and triggering harms to food, healthcare, water, sanitation, education, and housing. This is strong negative evidence that welfare was secondary to other priorities.  
  - IDs: `6B.1`, `5B.8`, `5B.6`, `5B.5`

- **DRC President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations** — Amnesty International, 2024-09-30, https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/  
  - Claim: Amnesty said Tshisekedi ignored the worsening human-rights situation, the state of siege militarized everyday life, and humanitarian needs for shelter, food, healthcare, and education remained chronically underfunded. That points to welfare being subordinated to coercive state control.  
  - IDs: `6B.1`, `5B.6`, `5B.7`, `5B.9`

- **More than 260 women sexually assaulted during Congo prison break, UN reports shows** — Reuters, 2024-09-12, https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/More-than-260-women-sexually-assaulted-during-Congo-prison-break-UN-reports-shows-47860482/  
  - Claim: Reuters reported prison guards used live fire during the Makala escape attempt, killing at least 129 people, and more than 260 women were sexually assaulted. This is severe evidence that the state was not organized around protecting human welfare in practice.  
  - IDs: `6B.1`, `6B.2`, `5B.9`

- **Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts: report** — Reuters, 2024-01-15, https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/  
  - Claim: A civil-society report said CENI could not account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement. This is indirect, but it is concrete evidence of public-resource handling that looks more like capture and mismanagement than welfare-first governance.  
  - IDs: `6B.1`, `5B.5`, `5B.9`

**Search Gap**  
I did not find a direct, ruler-specific 2024 audit showing that Tshisekedi consistently prioritized welfare over propaganda or patronage across health, sanitation, nutrition, and social protection. The strongest pro-welfare evidence is programmatic and selective, while the strongest counterevidence is systemic and operational: underfunded services, violent custody failures, and a militarized state of siege.
